title: PRA: Project Risk Analysis — PRA-package
text: Monte Carlo Simulation (mcs()) Propagates schedule cost uncertainty triangular distribution model using mc2d. Returns S3 object print, summary plot methods. Second Moment Method (smm()) Analytical first- second-moment propagation uncertainty without simulation. Returns S3 object print, summary plot methods. Earned Value Management (pv(), ev(), ac(), sv(), cv(), spi(), cpi(), eac(), etc(), tcpi(), vac()) Full suite EVM performance metrics forecasting functions. Contingency Analysis (contingency()) Derives cost schedule contingency simulation output user-specified confidence level. Sensitivity Analysis (sensitivity()) Ranks risk drivers contribution overall project uncertainty. Learning Curves (fit_sigmoidal(), predict_sigmoidal(), plot_sigmoidal()) Fits Pearl, Gompertz, Logistic sigmoidal growth models cumulative cost progress data using nonlinear least squares (minpack.lm). Bayesian Risk Inference (risk_prob(), risk_post_prob()) Beta-Binomial conjugate updating risk event probabilities. Correlation Matrices (cor_matrix()) Constructs valid positive-definite correlation matrices use multivariate simulations. Design Structure Matrix (parent_dsm(), grandparent_dsm()) Derives direct (parent) indirect (grandparent) dependency structure matrices binary adjacency matrix. Returns S3 object print, summary plot methods. Probabilistic Networks (prob_net(), prob_net_sim(), prob_net_learn(), prob_net_update()) Forward simulation Bayesian conditioning causal network risks, resources tasks. prob_net() returns S3 object print, summary plot methods.

code: # Set the number os simulations and the task distributions for a toy project. num_sims <- 10000 task_dists <- list(   list(type = "normal", mean = 10, sd = 2), # Task A: Normal distribution   list(type = "triangular", a = 5, b = 10, c = 15), # Task B: Triangular distribution   list(type = "uniform", min = 8, max = 12) # Task C: Uniform distribution )  # Set the correlation matrix for the correlations between tasks. cor_mat <- matrix(c(   1, 0.5, 0.3,   0.5, 1, 0.4,   0.3, 0.4, 1 ), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)  # Run the Monte Carlo simulation. results <- mcs(num_sims, task_dists, cor_mat)  # Calculate the contingency and print the results. contingency <- contingency(results, phigh = 0.95, pbase = 0.50) cat("Contingency based on 95th percentile and 50th percentile:", contingency) #> Contingency based on 95th percentile and 50th percentile: 6.850275  # Without correlation matrix results_indep <- mcs(num_sims, task_dists) contingency_indep <- contingency(results_indep,   phigh = 0.95,   pbase = 0.50 ) cat("Contingency based on 95th percentile and 50th percentile ( independent tasks):", contingency_indep) #> Contingency based on 95th percentile and 50th percentile ( #> independent tasks): 4.992183  # Build a barplot to visualize the contingency results. contingency_data <- data.frame(   Scenario = c("With Correlation", "Independent Tasks"),   Contingency = c(contingency, contingency_indep) ) barplot(   height = contingency_data$Contingency,   names = contingency_data$Scenario,   col = c("orange", "purple"),   horiz = TRUE,   xlab = "Contingency",   ylab = "Scenario" ) title("Contingency Calculation for Project Scenarios")
